title: "MFE Integration"
format: html
---

## Purpose

The BRDR alignment UI is available as reusable micro-frontends (MFE's) so another application can embed the alignment flow without rebuilding the full demo host viewer.

Available MFE routes:

- `/alignment-mfe.html`: GRB full workflow
- `/alignment-mfe-simple.html`: GRB compact workflow
- `/alignment-mfe-wfs.html`: BRK/WFS full workflow
- `/alignment-mfe-wfs-simple.html`: BRK/WFS compact workflow

## Integration Model

The current integration contract is based on an `iframe` plus `postMessage`.

Flow:

1. Host application loads the MFE in an `iframe`.
2. MFE emits `BRDR_ALIGNMENT_READY`.
3. Host sends the selected geometry and CRS using `BRDR_ALIGNMENT_INIT`.
4. User works in the MFE and clicks `Aanpassen`.
5. MFE emits `BRDR_ALIGNMENT_APPLY` with the aligned geometry.

The same MFE can be embedded same-origin or cross-origin, provided the host validates `event.origin` correctly and avoids mixed-content situations.

## Message Contract

### Host -> MFE

```ts
{
  type: "BRDR_ALIGNMENT_INIT",
  payload: {
    crs: "EPSG:31370" | "EPSG:3812" | "EPSG:28992",
    geometry: GeoJSONGeometry
  }
}
```

Optional update while the MFE stays open:

```ts
{
  type: "BRDR_ALIGNMENT_UPDATE_GEOMETRY",
  payload: {
    crs: "EPSG:31370" | "EPSG:3812" | "EPSG:28992",
    geometry: GeoJSONGeometry
  }
}
```

Important:

- send a GeoJSON **Geometry**, not a full `FeatureCollection`
- the coordinates must match the CRS you pass in `payload.crs`
- supported geometry types are `Point`, `MultiPoint`, `LineString`, `MultiLineString`, `Polygon`, `MultiPolygon`

### MFE -> Host

Ready event:

```ts
{ type: "BRDR_ALIGNMENT_READY" }
```

Apply event:

```ts
{
  type: "BRDR_ALIGNMENT_APPLY",
  payload: {
    geometry: GeoJSONGeometry
  }
}
```

## Minimal Example

```html
<iframe
  id="brdr-mfe"
  src="https://example.com/alignment-mfe.html"
  style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"
></iframe>

<script>
  const iframe = document.getElementById("brdr-mfe");
  const mfeOrigin = "https://example.com";

  const selectedGeometry = {
    type: "Polygon",
    coordinates: [[[674109.9, 679157.1], [674108.4, 679157.3], [674067.2, 679162.5], [674109.9, 679157.1]]]
  };

  window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
    if (event.origin !== mfeOrigin) return;
    const msg = event.data;
    if (!msg || typeof msg !== "object") return;

    if (msg.type === "BRDR_ALIGNMENT_READY") {
      iframe.contentWindow.postMessage(
        {
          type: "BRDR_ALIGNMENT_INIT",
          payload: {
            crs: "EPSG:3812",
            geometry: selectedGeometry
          }
        },
        mfeOrigin
      );
    }

    if (msg.type === "BRDR_ALIGNMENT_APPLY") {
      const alignedGeometry = msg.payload.geometry;
      console.log("Aligned geometry", alignedGeometry);
    }
  });
</script>
```

## Same-Origin and Cross-Origin Notes

- Same-origin embedding works directly.
- Cross-origin embedding is supported in the MFE handshake.
- If the host runs on `https`, the MFE should also be served on `https`.
- `https` host + `http` MFE will be blocked by browsers as mixed content.

## Full vs Compact Variants

Choose the route based on the host use case:

- **full**: chart + step navigation + more context
- **compact**: faster selection of predictions with a simplified side panel

## Alternative to iframe

The project also contains React components for direct integration into another React app, but the ready-to-use public contract today is the iframe-based MFE integration.

Key files:

- `src/alignmentMfeApp.tsx`
- `src/components/alignment/BrdrAlignmentViewer.tsx`
- `src/components/alignment/BrdrCompactAlignmentViewer.tsx`
